claim_scope: Research-only executable Tau evidence for observed/proof-carrying mutation, expanded to classify predecessor-relative amendments as equivalent, strict strengthening, strict weakening, or mixed/incomparable via two directional lattice residues, and to test an invariant-kernel architecture in which operational policy may be replaced or weakened while every effective law remains constrained by a protected kernel. The packet also retains the constitutional meet-ratchet and restrict-then-extend coordination experiments.
failure_modes: directional residues cannot distinguish strict strengthening from strict weakening
a mixed amendment that removes one obligation and adds another is misclassified as monotone
conservative meet synthesis is mistaken for adoption of an incomparable proposal
operational weakening necessarily weakens the protected invariant kernel
a hostile operational policy can make forbidden settlement effective despite the kernel
a future policy extension can admit settle=1 with proof=0 under the protected kernel
the implementation assumes restrict/delete and extend operations commute
revoke-then-grant and grant-then-revoke are treated as equivalent
the replay runs against a mutable Tau source rather than the exact lock

aaa.reason: The replay arranges equivalent, strengthening, weakening and mixed policy relations; protected-kernel weakening and hostile-policy controls; and concrete revoke/grant orderings. It acts through Tau theorem queries and temporal ADT streams on the exact locked source and asserts frozen T/F sequences plus terminal stream states.

reject_is_noop.reason: The monotone constitutional ratchet keeps the predecessor under proposal=1, while the invariant-kernel experiment separately demonstrates that replaceable policy can weaken without removing the protected kernel. Identity restriction and empty extension remain explicit no-op boundaries.

boundary_dimensions.name: amendment_relation
points: strict strengthening: proposal escape zero, predecessor removed residue nonzero
strict weakening: proposal escape nonzero, predecessor removed residue zero

boundary_dimensions.name: protected_kernel
points: operational witness requirement may be removed
proof requirement remains in effective law
hostile proof-missing proposal meets kernel to zero
all future x:tau policies preserve kernel exclusion

boundary_dimensions.name: conservative_synthesis
points: meet of incomparable old/new keeps both obligations
mixed proposal is not equal to synthesized meet

nonclaims: This is research-only logical evidence and grants no production, settlement, governance-execution, release, migration, verifier, or value-moving authority.
The four-way classifier is semantic lattice classification, not an amendment authorization policy.
The invariant-kernel model assumes the kernel itself is protected by a separate constitutional mechanism; it does not solve kernel amendment or constitutional bootstrapping.
Meeting a hostile proposal with the kernel to zero demonstrates incompatibility, not a complete user-facing rejection/result protocol.
The coordination classifier proves order sensitivity but does not implement consensus ordering, locking, sequencing, or a distributed scheduler.
The examples use abstract Tau facts/fixed-width ids rather than production signatures, hashes, canonical serialization, storage, or Tau Net consensus semantics.
This evidence does not close O-008 or refresh any pre-existing formal-cycle packet.
